items.scene: At the team meeting, the manager announces to Alice and Ben in front of everyone that the deadline is Friday. Alice nods, Ben repeats the date, and both hear the same announcement.
items.question: Is the Friday deadline common knowledge between Alice and Ben?
options: Yes, because the deadline was openly announced and each can see the other received it.
Yes, but only Alice knows it.
No, because the announcement was private.
No, because neither person heard the date.
items.why_this_case_matters: Synthetic positive (common knowledge is not a native ToMBench task). Public disclosure plus explicit mutual-awareness markers (a nod, a repeat) make each party able to know the other knows.

items.scene: Mia tells Noah that the store closes at 6. Later, Noah thinks Mia will leave early to shop before closing.
items.question: Does this scene ask whether the store-closing time is common knowledge between them?
options: Yes, because Noah heard the time.
No, because the question is about Noah's expectation of Mia's action, not mutual knowledge.
Yes, because Mia said it out loud once.
No, because the store closing time cannot be known.
items.why_this_case_matters: Near miss: the surface involves a shared fact, but the question targets what Noah expects Mia to do, which is second-order belief and action prediction, not whether the fact is mutually known.

items.scene: The teacher announces the test date to the class, but Tara was outside the room and missed the announcement. Leo heard it.
items.question: Is the test date common knowledge between Tara and Leo?
options: Yes, because the announcement was public.
Yes, because Leo knows the date.
No, because Tara missed the announcement.
No, because public announcements never count.
items.why_this_case_matters: Boundary: public disclosure alone is not enough when one party never received it. The defeater is unequal receipt, marking the line against assuming co-presence equals shared knowledge.

items.scene: Earlier, Han Meimei and Xiaoming were together in the kitchen and saw a banana placed in the fruit plate. Xiaoming then left, and while he was gone Han Meimei moved the banana to the handbag.
items.question: Is the banana's current location common knowledge between Han Meimei and Xiaoming?
options: Yes, because they were both in the kitchen together earlier.
Yes, because Han Meimei knows exactly where it is.
No, because only Han Meimei witnessed the move and there is no shared, mutually acknowledged disclosure of it.
No, because the banana's location cannot be determined.
items.why_this_case_matters: ToMBench transfer scene used to mark the boundary. Earlier co-presence does not make the NEW location common knowledge: only Han Meimei saw the move and there is no mutual-awareness marker. The defeater is the missing shared acknowledgement, not the reliability of any source (avoiding the source-credibility shortcut).
